traits.notes: The seedling exhibits a distinctive whorled leaf arrangement at the apex. The stem is notably thick and segmented. Several leaves display damage in the form of holes and ragged edges. An orange tag is tied around the stem, likely for identification purposes.

data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves, appearing to be 5-7, radiate from a single terminal node at the stem apex, clearly visible in all images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are arranged in a dense rosette-like cluster at the stem tip)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3.	Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (individual leaves are undivided blades)
    4.	Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5.	Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6.	Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7.	Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins appear smooth, though some leaves show irregular holes/damage)
    8.	Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): obovate to elliptic (leaves are broadest above the middle and taper towards the base)
    9.	Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): obtuse to shortly acuminate (tips are generally rounded but can be slightly pointed)
    10.	Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (tapers gradually to the petiole)
    11.	Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single midrib with lateral veins branching off)
    12.	Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, prominent, spaced relatively evenly, curving towards the leaf margin (arcuate)
    13.	Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): glabrous, shiny (surface appears smooth and reflects light)
    14.	Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on leaf surface)
    15.	Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are distinct but relatively short compared to leaf blade size)
    16.	Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17.	Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears thick, rigid, and segmented/ringed, indicative of a woody seedling)
    18.	Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem surface appears smooth where visible)
    19.	Stem color: green with white/greyish markings (visible in images 1 and 3)
    20.	Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): ridged (stem shows distinct horizontal rings or striations)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21.	Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at the leaf nodes)
    22.	Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23.	Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint visible at leaf base)
    24.	Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: The seedling exhibits a distinctive whorled leaf arrangement at the apex. The stem is notably thick and segmented. Several leaves display damage in the form of holes and ragged edges. An orange tag is tied around the stem, likely for identification purposes.
